subtype: Approach: planning for the holidays with a neighbour [Thinking]
passage: Note from Sabina, next-door neighbour. Hansa knocked on our door on Saturday with a list. Her family leaves for a week on Monday, and she asked whether I could water her pots each morning. She had already moved all six pots together beside our shared wall. "So you only walk a few steps," she explained. On a card she had written how much water each pot gets. When I asked why she was planning so early, she said, "A week is a long time for a thirsty plant." I said yes, and pinned the card inside my kitchen door. - Sabina

qa.q: How many pots did Hansa move together?
qa.a: Hansa moved all six pots together beside the shared wall.

qa.q: What might Hansa have been worried about before the trip?
qa.a: Hansa was probably worried about the plants going thirsty while the family is away, which is why she planned early.

qa.q: What else could Hansa do to support the neighbour, and why?
qa.a: Hansa could leave a family phone number and a watering can in an easy spot, so the neighbour can ask if something looks wrong.

qa.q: How does Sabina see Hansa's request?
qa.a: Sabina finds it well prepared and easy to say yes to, since the pots are grouped and the card explains the watering.

grounding: A girl who knows her family will be away for a week arranges for a neighbour to water the pots and groups them together.
